paper_title: Counterfactual Influence as a Distributional Quantity
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates Spearman’s R correlation for the quantity I(xₜ → xₜ) as a function of the number of models M, presented on a logarithmic scale. The x-axis is labeled “Number of models M (log)” and spans from 25 to 500, with tick marks at regular intervals of 25 (i.e., 25, 50, 100, 250, 500). The y-axis is labeled “Spearman’s R correlation for I(xₜ → xₜ)” and ranges from 0.90 to 1.00. A single solid blue line with circular markers connects five data points, showing a consistent upward trend. At the start of the x-axis (M=25), the correlation value is approximately 0.953, and at the end (M=500), it reaches approximately 0.997. The line increases steadily across the entire range, with intermediate values at M=50 (≈0.967), M=100 (≈0.983), and M=250 (≈0.992).
